newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia, Hungary see agreement on Gabcikovo dam.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia, Hungary see agreement on Gabcikovo dam.

text.p: Slovakia and Hungary see hope of a settlement of their row over Slovakia's decision to divert Danube waters in a dam project, a Slovak government official said on Monday.

The countries are in dispute over Slovakia's decision to unilateraly divert a considerable part of the Danube waters for its Gabcikovo dam project after Hungary quit a joint deal which planned a similar dam at Nagymaros in Hungary.
Slovakia claims Hungary breached its contract while the Hungarians say diverting the water breaks international law.
They had agreed to bring their case to the International Court in the Hague, which is due to consider it next year.

But Magda Pospisilova, spokeswoman for Slovak Premier Vladimir Meciar, told journalists at the end of an informal bilateral meeting between Meciar and Hungary's premier Gyula Horn on Monday: "Both sides think that there is room for an out-of-court settlement of the Gabcikovo-Nagymaros problem."
"Mr. Horn said several Slovak proposals were sympathetic and that he could see areas of agreement on the Gabcikovo issue," Pospisilova said.
Meciar and Horn met after a trilateral meeting of the heads of government of Austria, Hungary and Slovakia in the west Slovak spa town of Piestany.

At the end of that meeting Horn, Meciar and Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky issued a statement in which they pledged to increase cooperation in battling organised crime, illegal migration and nuclear smuggling.
They also agreed to begin work on coordinated efforts to prevent money laundering and cross-boundary trafic.

The three heads of governments also reviewed progress made in areas of cooperation in the energy sectors, development of transport infrastructure, joint ventures, industrial parks and cooperation between their Danube ports.
